records.old: Structured Derivation of Heron's Formula (15 min): Learners follow a teacher-guided derivation on the board, filling in a structured notes scaffold (gaps provided on a printed or ARES-displayed template). The derivation steps are: Step 1 — Recall Area = ½ab sin C. Step 2 — From the cosine rule, cos C = (a² + b² − c²) / 2ab, so sin²C = 1 − cos²C. Step 3 — Substitute and simplify to show Area² = [s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)] where s = (a+b+c)/2 is the semi-perimeter. Step 4 — Take the square root to obtain Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]. The teacher does the first two steps fully; learners complete steps 3 and 4 in pairs. PART B — Worked Example with the Maize Plot (10 min): Teacher works one full example on the board using Mwangi's farm (a=40, b=55, c=63): compute s = (40+55+63)/2 = 79; then s−a=39, s−b=24, s−c=16; Area = √(79×39×24×16) = √(1,183,104) ≈ 1,087.7 m². Teacher narrates each step aloud. PART C — Group Practice (10 min)

records.old: Each group of 4 receives: one sharpened hexagonal pencil, one sheet of plain paper, a ruler, and a protractor. Learners roll the pencil on the paper and trace its hexagonal cross-section, producing a regular hexagon.
records.new: Each group of 4 receives: a hexagonal pencil (to look at), a sheet of plain paper, a ruler, a compass and a protractor. Learners notice that the end of the pencil is a regular hexagon but too small to measure (sides about 4 mm), so they construct a large one: draw a circle of radius 5 cm, keep the compass opening at 5 cm, step it around the circle to mark six points, and join the points to make a regular hexagon of side 5 cm.
records.why: Rolling a pencil does not trace a hexagon (it traces a straight line), the sharpened end is a cone, and a pencil's hexagonal end has sides of only about 4 mm, too small to measure with a ruler and protractor to the stated ±2 mm and ±2°. A compass-constructed hexagon (radius = side, a standard construction) needs only a geometrical set. Teacher must decide whether all groups have compasses; if not, a printed hexagon of side 5 cm works equally well.

value.criterion: Choosing and justifying the correct formula
value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Selects the correct formula for every shape and explains clearly, using the available measurements, why it is the practical choice when no height can be measured.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Selects the correct formula for most shapes and gives a reasonable but incomplete reason.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Chooses formulas incorrectly or without giving a reason.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Shows correctly how h = b sin C leads to ½ab sin C, and links the parallelogram, equilateral triangle, hexagon and pentagon formulas to the triangle formulas with clear steps and angles.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Gives most steps of the derivations, with a small gap in the angles or in the link between formulas.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: States formulas without showing how they are derived or connected.

value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Calculations are correct and fully shown (Heron's ≈ 1,087.7 m², stage ≈ 21.75 m², pentagon ≈ 139.4 cm²), with units and sensible rounding.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Method is correct but with a minor arithmetic, rounding or unit error.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Method is incorrect or the working is not shown.

value.criterion: Connecting to the Kericho courtyard and driving question
value.excellent: Exceeds Expectations: Clearly explains how the formulas let the contractor find every area from measurable data and avoid over- or under-ordering, including rounding up tile counts.
value.proficient: Meets Expectations: Links the formulas to the courtyard but gives limited detail on ordering material.
value.developing: Approaches Expectations: Gives little or no link to the courtyard or the driving question.

records.why: The contract allows only three level fields, so the fourth CBE level, Below Expectations, cannot be represented in the rubric. Suggestion: teachers treat any response that does not reach Approaches Expectations as Below Expectations; the template owner may want to add a fourth level field.

records.reference: KICD Grade 10 curriculum design, Mathematics (Core), Sub-Strand 2.5 Area of Polygons; no Essential Mathematics design available
records.why: No KICD source for Essential Mathematics is available here: the Mathematics PDF in the project is the Core design (where this topic is Sub-Strand 2.5, 14 lessons, with 7 outcomes covering quadrilaterals, heptagon/octagon and irregular polygons, and two key inquiry questions), so no KICD wording was restored. Please check outcomes (a)-(e), the key inquiry question 'How are areas of polygons useful?', the competencies and values against the Essential Mathematics design. Two details look suspicious: outcome (a) says 'included acute angle' while Core says only 'included angle' (and Lesson 5 uses a 110° angle), and the strand/sub-strand number 2.4 (Core numbers it 2.5) cannot be confirmed. Content taught but not clearly in the outcomes: rhombus base × height (now covered in Lesson 5 decision rule).
